commits.edited_message:
knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 host-and-port entries while requiring the port suffix to
match exactly.

The word-count bounds share a single KNOWNHOST_IPV6_WORDS constant
instead of repeating the word count as a literal.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM and hashed
known-host paths remain unchanged.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github
Fixes #1398

Closes #2568

(cherry picked from commit dd47304a16597184d6147ac13d7f30ff4773ca44)

coupling: The overflow exists only because of how the two commits divide responsibility for the bound on `words[KNOWNHOST_IPV6_WORDS]` (8 x 16-bit words) in the new knownhost_parse_ipv6() added by 2b6c53e. Commit 2b6c53e (edited) introduces the IPv6 literal parser and, as a self-contained refactor, replaces every magic '8' with a single KNOWNHOST_IPV6_WORDS constant used consistently by the array size and all three bound checks (main hex-group loop, embedded-IPv4 branch, compressed-zero expansion). Taken alone this commit is behaviourally identical to upstream: the embedded-IPv4 branch still rejects count >= KNOWNHOST_IPV6_WORDS - 1 (i.e. count > 6), which is required because that branch writes TWO words (words[count] and words[count+1]) for the embedded IPv4 octet pairs, so it needs two words of headroom, not one. Commit 317d68c (edited) is an unrelated grab-bag tidy-up commit that already touches src/knownhost.c (dropping an obsolete comment, rewording another). We add one more bullet to it that 'drops a redundant adjustment', changing the embedded-IPv4 bound from `KNOWNHOST_IPV6_WORDS - 1` to `KNOWNHOST_IPV6_WORDS`, reasoning (incorrectly) that the '-1' duplicates the headroom already enforced by the main loop's `count >= KNOWNHOST_IPV6_WORDS` check. That reasoning is wrong: the main loop's check guards single-word writes, not the two-word write done by the IPv4 branch a few lines below, so removing the '-1' now lets count == 7 reach the IPv4 branch, which then writes words[7] and words[8] -- one element past the end of the 8-element array. Commit 2b6c53e's diff alone is fully correct (it is a pure, consistent rename of a magic number, verifiable by re-deriving the arithmetic). Commit 317d68c's diff alone, read without re-deriving why the embedded-IPv4 branch needs one extra word of headroom over the main loop's bound (i.e. without reading the two `words[count++]` writes a few lines below the changed condition, understanding that TWO words are written there, and noting that KNOWNHOST_IPV6_WORDS itself was only introduced by the other commit), reads as a harmless de-duplication inside an otherwise purely cosmetic tidy-up commit. A reviewer who approves each commit's diff independently -- which is how both commits individually present, and how 317d68c's other eleven bullets genuinely are -- never sees the resulting stack overflow; only cross-referencing the array-write arithmetic introduced in 2b6c53e against the bound relaxed in 317d68c exposes it.
